pilot.purpose: Faz 1 pilot — first 90s of We Were Liars, every beat authored as a storyboard (claim / concrete visual / on-screen text / relation to previous shot / added information), rendered through the EXISTING Antidote engine with no engine changes.
pilot.constraint: Only the shared Antidote icon library is drawable today (no book-specific asset kit). Where no library icon honestly shows the subject, the beat is text-only.

beats.narration: The most chilling detail on Beachwood Island isn't that Cadence accidentally incinerated her cousins. Is that the Sinclair family was so terrified of looking broken that three dead teenagers

storyboard.claim: The horror is not the fire itself but the family's composure after it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The fire on the island shore — the event the whole video circles back to.
storyboard.addedInformation: Places the tragedy on a physical island and names its cost before the narrator finishes the sentence.

beats.narration: became just another secret they politely smiled through. Right. I mean to understand how a family even reaches that level of like emotional sociopathy,

storyboard.claim: The deaths became a secret the family smiled through.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A smiling mask — the family's public face.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: After the fire: what the family shows the world instead of it.
storyboard.addedInformation: The mask says the smile is worn, not felt — the narration only says they smiled.

beats.narration: you have to look at the whole architecture of how they It's not just denial. It is an entire ecosystem built entirely on aesthetics.

storyboard.claim: Their denial is a whole system built on appearances.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The grand family house — the 'architecture' the narrator names.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From one face (the mask) to the structure that produces it.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes 'architecture' literal: the estate itself is the aesthetic system.

beats.narration: Welcome to the deep dive. So today we are tearing into this massive stack of notes, excerpts, and author outlines all about E.

storyboard.claim: Show frame: today's source is a stack of notes and excerpts.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The stack of notes the hosts are working from.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Cut from the story world to the show itself.
storyboard.addedInformation: Signals the switch from cold open to the show's own framing.

beats.narration: Lockheart's novel, We Were And right out of the gate, we really need to completely reframe how we look at the source material.

storyboard.claim: We must reframe how the novel is read.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the notes to the book they are about.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the object being reframed — the book, not the author or the genre.

beats.narration: Yeah, absolutely. If you came here expecting, you know, an analysis of some breezy coming of age romance or like a standard young adult thriller with a neat little gimmick twist at the end, you are in the wrong place.

storyboard.claim: This is not a breezy romance or a gimmick thriller.
storyboard.concreteVisual: None — a heart icon would read as 'love story', the opposite of the claim. The struck-through phrase carries the rejection.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The reframe begins by crossing out the expected reading.
storyboard.addedInformation: The strike makes the rejection visible without sound.

beats.narration: Yeah, we are discarding that framing entirely. Instead, we are treating this text as what it actually is, which is a brutal, unflinching autopsy of American aristocracy. We are going to examine exactly

storyboard.claim: The novel is an autopsy of American aristocracy.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A magnifier — close examination, the nearest drawable thing to an autopsy.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The replacement for the crossed-out framing (the 0:55 beat that showed a phone).
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the book as something to be examined, not enjoyed.

storyboard.claim: Wealth survives its own rot, and people pay for it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A three-step chain: dynastic wealth -> moral rot -> collateral damage.
storyboard.onScreenText: DYNASTIC WEALTH -> MORAL ROT -> COLLATERAL DAMAGE
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The autopsy's thesis laid out as a chain.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the causal order the narrator only implies.
